tldr: Lingma SWE-GPT is an open-source LLM series (7B and 72B) trained on simulated real-world software development processes, achieving competitive performance with closed-source models on automated software issue resolution.
contributions: Introduced Lingma SWE-GPT, an open-source model series optimized for automated software improvement
Proposed a development process-centric training approach capturing dynamic tool usage, reasoning, and interactive problem-solving
Demonstrated effectiveness on SWE-bench Lite and Verified with significant improvements over existing open-source models
Provided insights into fault localization capabilities and performance consistency
methods: The authors collected ~90,000 pull requests from 4,000 public GitHub repositories (with 50+ stars, non-overlapping with SWE-bench), filtered by heuristics including PRs modifying 1-5 code files and excluding test-only changes. They then synthesized development process data using a three-stage workflow (SWESynInfer): repository understanding (using Repo Structure, Navigate Repo, and Code Compressor tools), fault localization (using search APIs with AST-based context retrieval), and patch generation (with git operations and lint-based iterative debugging). The model was trained via a development process-centric iterative strategy using curriculum learning and rejection sampling to retain high-quality instances.
results: Lingma SWE-GPT 72B resolves 30.20% of issues on SWE-bench Verified (22.76% relative improvement over Llama 3.1 405B), approaching GPT-4o's 31.80% resolution rate. Lingma SWE-GPT 7B resolves 18.20% of issues, surpassing Llama 3.1 70B's 17.20%.
limitations: The approach depends on publicly available GitHub data and may not generalize to private or proprietary codebases. The dataset filtering (e.g., requiring English content, limiting PRs to 1-5 modified files) may exclude certain types of software changes. Performance still trails closed-source models like GPT-4o slightly (30.20% vs 31.80%). The model relies on simulated development processes generated by AutoCodeRover framework, which may not fully capture all aspects of real developer workflows.
